SBE order entry and private data
Last update: September 30, 2026
OKX plans to introduce Simple Binary Encoding (SBE) services for order entry and private order and fill updates. The services are expected to launch in the demo trading environment in early November 2026 and in the production environment in early December 2026 .
Existing REST and JSON WebSocket APIs will remain unaffected.
New SBE services
Service Production URL Demo trading URL XML schema Order entry wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe Download Private data wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe Download
The login method is the same as that of the existing SBE Market Data service . Authentication is completed during the WebSocket HTTP Upgrade request by providing the API key and signature in the request headers.
JSON control messages use text frames with opcode 1 , while SBE messages use binary frames with opcode 2 .
Compared with the JSON services, the fields in SBE messages are streamlined. Refer to the XML schemas for the complete message layouts and field definitions.
SBE order entry
The order entry service will support the following operations:
Place order and place multiple orders Amend order and amend multiple orders Cancel order and cancel multiple orders
Batch operations will support up to 20 orders. SBE order entry will support CASH and CROSS trading modes. Clients that require another trading mode should continue to use the JSON WebSocket trading API.
SBE private data
The private data service will support the following channels:
orders : Publishes an update when an order is created or its state changes. fills : Publishes order-book fill events and is available to VIP4 and above users.
Neither channel will publish an initial snapshot. Subscription requests and responses will remain in JSON format, while channel data will be encoded in SBE. The orders channel will support filtering by instType ; instIdCode is not required. For the fills channel, instIdCode is also not required.

Signal Clone — New API endpoint
Last update: May 14, 2026
OKX is adding API support for the Signal Clone (Order Sharing) feature. API traders can now generate a universal sharing link programmatically by passing an order ID. The link encodes the order parameters (instrument, side, leverage, price, TP/SL, etc.) server-side. Recipients who open the link will have those parameters prefilled in the OKX App trading panel.
This feature is scoped to USDT-margined perpetual contracts. Signal Clone must be enabled for the account.
Create signal link
Create signal link
A new endpoint POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link is added. Pass orderId and instId in the request body. The order must belong to the requesting account. Only USDT-margined perpetual contracts ( instId ending in -USDT-SWAP ) are supported. Other instrument types will return an error. Returns a shortLink — a universal OKX App link that can be shared with others to prefill the trading panel with the order parameters. Rate limit: 10 requests per second per user.
Request example
POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link
body { "orderId" : "3556007031710728192" , "instId" : "ADA-USDT-SWAP" }
Request parameters
Parameter Type Required Description orderId String Yes Order ID. Must belong to the requesting account. instId String Yes Instrument ID, e.g. BTC-USDT-SWAP . Only USDT-margined perpetuals are supported.
Response example
{ "code" : "0" , "data" : [ { "shortLink" : "https://www.okx.com/ul/1xJ7nV" } ], "msg" : "" }
Response parameters
Parameter Type Description shortLink String Universal sharing link. Recipients can open this link in the OKX App to have the order parameters prefilled in the trading panel.

https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en#upcom.title: WebSocket port 8443 discontinuation
https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en#upcom.content:
WebSocket port 8443 discontinuation
Last update: September 30, 2026
To support a network infrastructure upgrade, OKX will stop accepting WebSocket connections on port 8443 on October 31, 2026 . Port 443 already works on all affected domains, and both ports remain available until then.
Breaking change
After October 31, 2026 , connections to port 8443 will fail. Remove :8443 from your WebSocket URLs. Only the port changes; the host and path stay the same. wss:// uses port 443 by default, and :443 also works. This applies to every path, including /ws/v5/public , /ws/v5/private and /ws/v5/business .
Production Before: wss://ws.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public After: wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/public Demo trading Before: wss://wspap.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public After: wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/public
REST API and Colo connections are not affected.
